behaviors.what: Anyone can call releaseSponsorPrize() once status is CashWon or Refunding; there is no caller check. It sends the escrowed NFT to sponsorRecipient with a plain ERC-721 transferFrom (Raffle.sol:404), not safeTransferFrom, so the recipient's onERC721Received hook is never called. The only check afterwards is prizeToken.ownerOf(prizeTokenId) == recipient (Raffle.sol:405). prizeClaimed is set to true before the transfer (Raffle.sol:403), so after a successful delivery the function can never run again. This NFT path also skips the payout-time protocol-destination check that every quote-token payout goes through (_transferQuote, Raffle.sol:564-567). Prize escrow at creation uses safeTransferFrom (RaffleFactory.sol:128) and ticket mints use _safeMint (Raffle.sol:235). The winner's NFT delivery also uses plain transferFrom (Raffle.sol:334-337), but there the winner must be the caller, so only the sponsor-side delivery can be triggered by a third party.

behaviors.whyItMatters: The docs describe a checked return of the prize to the sponsor side: IRaffle.sol:354 "Returns the escrowed prize to the immutable sponsor recipient after `CashWon` or `Refunding`."; IRaffle.sol:299 "Raised when the prize token does not report the expected owner after transfer."; IRaffle.sol:32 "Full ticket refunds are enabled and the sponsor may recover the prize NFT."; DESIGN.md "Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize." Only an event parameter (IRaffle.sol:174, "Address that triggered the permissionless release.") hints that a third party can choose when this happens. Nothing says the return skips the recipient's ERC-721 acceptance check. Example: sponsorRecipient is a contract that records NFTs only in onERC721Received (a vault or pool), or one that cannot move ERC-721s at all (a USDC splitter). Any stranger can push the NFT into it unrecorded or unrecoverable, and the claim flag blocks any second attempt. A safe transfer would have reverted and left the prize in escrow. Impact is limited to contract recipients, so severity is low. A narrow corollary: sponsorRecipient is checked against the raffle registry only at creation (RaffleFactory.sol:166), and only if it already has code (Raffle.sol:602). Clones are deployed with CREATE (packages/contracts/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/Clones.sol:57), so their addresses are predictable. If a sponsor names a future clone address as recipient, releaseSponsorProceeds later reverts with InvalidQuoteDestination (Raffle.sol:565), but releaseSponsorPrize still moves the NFT into that other clone. That contradicts DESIGN.md "Never move assets between raffle clones." This requires the sponsor's own misconfiguration and harms only the sponsor.
